newsitem.title: FRANCE: France shaves interest rates after EU deal.
newsitem.headline: France shaves interest rates after EU deal.

text.p: The Bank of France trimmed two key interest rates on Tuesday in a further move to boost France's economy after European Union countries agreed last Friday on a pact limiting budget deficits under a future single currency.

The independent central bank shaved its intervention rate, which sets a floor on money market rates, to 3.15 percent from 3.20 percent. It cut is five-to-10 rate, which sets the ceiling, to 4.60 percent from 4.75 percent.
The rate cut, effective from Thursday December 19, was announced after a meeting earlier on Tuesday of the Bank's monetary policy council.
Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet was due to give the annual presentation of monetary policy later on Tuesday.

Economists had said they expected the Bank to ease rates in the coming weeks after an agreement this weekend among European Union leaders on a budget discipline pact to reinforce fiscal rigour after the launch of monetary union.
